note: LEDGER THROUGHPUT MEASURED, so nobody needs to again. Ledger::commit on an M1 Max (8P+2E, loadavg 3-5): 721K facts/s on one core into a 500K-fact ledger, 999K/s into an empty one, 4.28M/s aggregate across 8 threads with independent ledgers. It degrades with ledger size: 665K/s marginal at 1M, 274K/s at 10M, about 600 bytes per fact resident. The read side is far cheaper - find(predicate) posting-list sweep 30.5M facts/s, value_of point query 1.95M/s, World deserialize 2.6M facts/s at 633 MiB/s. THE POINT: a full seed-42 genesis emits 13,533 facts in 1.97 s, about 6,900 facts/s, roughly 1 percent of one core capacity. The ledger is ~100x faster than anything that feeds it, so any plan to speed worldgen or the census by making fact commits cheaper is attacking 1 percent of the cost - profile the per-cell path instead. Agrees from the other end with the Sexton finding that census cost is 95 percent metric extraction. METHOD NOTE: measure from a throwaway crate outside the workspace, because std::time::Instant is banned in workspace test code by clippy.toml. TRAP: timing a thread scope charges ledger TEARDOWN to commit - freeing 4M facts took 6.1 s against 0.94 s to create them, which made threads look like they did not scale at all until the timer moved inside the loop.
